name: Calibration assumptions
statement: For the 'estimated' calibration, the scatter per record (σe) and the shift per group (σu) are estimated by code from each analysis's frozen records with Henderson's method III, fixed at the rules lock: fit the locked model (RSS_R, rank r_R) and the same model with one intercept per group (RSS_F, rank r_F); σe² = RSS_F / (N - r_F); σu² = max(0, (RSS_R - RSS_F - (r_F - r_R) σe²) / tr(Z'M_R Z)). A negative estimate set to zero is recorded with its value before truncation. Not estimable (N <= r_F, RSS_F zero, or the trace zero): the estimated calibration of that analysis is 'unavailable' with the reason, and the fixed one is still reported. No person or agent chooses a value. A flag, never a gate.

name: What no plan can ever do to the primary set
statement: These hold for every plan, including any plan written by a model; no plan setting can change them. (1) An exact duplicate is never counted twice: one record of the group, chosen by the survivor rule, enters. (2) No record connected to a definite conflict ever enters, under any plan: not both records, not one. That includes a record linked by exact duplicates to a record in conflict (the whole connected group stays out). A survivor's value is counted only in the sensitivity analysis 'conflicts_survivor_value'. (3) A physically invalid value never enters. (4) A group whose identity cannot be resolved (several candidates) never enters; it is counted separately only in the sensitivity analysis 'possible_duplicates_separate'. (5) A model-recalled record never enters. (6) A constructed record (the controlled extract) never enters a run that is not marked as a test. (7) A record without a group under the plan's grouping never enters (no group is invented; entry 'records_without_group'). A plan that tries (1) to (4) is refused at the rules lock and refused again when its rules are applied; (5) is refused by the database; (6) by code at record storage, inclusion and the freeze; (7) by the eligibility rule 'group_unknown'. The one plan choice that remains: possible duplicates counted once (the default) or both counted. They are also enforced on the frozen set itself: at the dataset freeze, code checks the primary set against each of (1) to (7), using the Checks flags (paper identity and physical validity computed independently of the plan's grouping and outcome) and each record's kind, source and, for (7), group under the plan's grouping, and refuses the freeze, logging the refusal, if any fails.

name: A Curator value takes effect only when a person accepts it
statement: A proposal that passed the checks takes effect only when a person accepts it (`hypocurate sources accept <proposal> --by <name>`; one decision per proposal, with the database's time; the command line takes the name as given and has no login). `seal-curation` seals the accepted values only, with quote, document, line, proposal, model and settings version, acceptor and time, as curation.json in a new sealed source version; rejected, refused, unanswered and not-stated proposals are left out (the field stays unassigned). Two accepted proposals for one field are not sealed. A curation file is checked against the version it is attached to before it is sealed (registration, seal-curation) and before it is applied: the base version's fingerprint must be that of the version's own files without the curation file; every quote must be found again in that version's documentation on the stated line with the stated term, and every value and term must pass the current checks; the acceptance fields must be present and valid. Anything else refuses the whole version. The validator does not prove that an approval is authentic: a well-formed file naming another acceptor passes it. The exact approved bytes are protected by the manifest fingerprint (the file the owner froze in data/, registered with its own base), and a newly sealed export rests on the accepted decisions recorded in the database where the curation happened. Adapters apply a curated value to every record of the version only where the record's field is not reported (never over a reported, converted or decided value), as 'assigned from source' with that citation. Runs use the newest sealed version; a run never calls the Curator. Values 'assigned by decision' stay owner decisions.

name: What happens when an agent request fails
statement: Every agent request is reserved, sent once (litellm's retries off) outside any database transaction, and recorded. At most two requests per agent call: an unavailable provider (connection error, timeout, 429, 5xx, or a reply litellm cannot read) is tried once more with the same request; an unusable answer (empty, malformed, a tool call, truncated at the output limit, longer than the role allows) once more with a fixed corrective note naming the failure code and, when the role's check gives one, its specific reason in code's own words (counts, the role's own keys, scope parts, names and rules; never the answer's text, a provider's text or an error's text), each attempt's reason stored with the stage, or the curation's summary, as 'attempt_reasons' (owner, 2026-10-10); refused credentials (401, 403), another refused request (4xx), a refusal, a cost the provider did not report, a reservation that cannot be written (nothing is sent), a failed recording on any branch (after a provider failure, a reply without usage or a usable reply) and every spending refusal stop at once. A failed call is recorded with no usage and counts at its maximum cost; a call whose recording fails stays 'started' and counts at its maximum cost. No provider, library or database text is kept with a call or sent in a later request; the process log gets the failure code, the exception's types and where it was raised, never its text. Not covered: what a library logs by itself (litellm's own debug logging is off unless a process turns it on). DSPy's JSON fallback is off. Step 8b: a role's own check of an answer that could be read gives a code that is corrected once the same way: 'invalid_plan' (Planner), 'numbers_unmatched' and 'wording_refused' (Analyst). The Analyst's 'unknown_name' and 'digit_outside_placeholder' are corrected once the same way.

name: What the Planner may answer and what code does with it
statement: The Planner answers one JSON object of fixed form: whether the claim belongs to the domain, the claim's scope (alloy classes, phase classes, test types, temperature bands with their ranges), and for each scope part whether the claim states it (true) or the Planner used the default (false), a mark code requires (a part marked as the default must hold the profile's default, else the answer is an invalid plan; the marks are otherwise the Planner's reading, not verified by code), the outcome field, exclusion rules from the menu, and a narrower scope that should be null (code decides any narrower scope; one given anyway is stored and never used); values from fixed lists only, no free text and no other key. Code builds the plan from the profile's defaults and only these parameters: the model, the eligibility rules, the calibration and the sufficiency option never come from the model, and of the rules only one does: for a band other than room temperature, the Planner's temperature range becomes the plan's temperature-range rule. The Planner's scope and exclusion rules decide which records are eligible. An answer whose shape, values or plan are not valid is corrected once, naming the code and its specific reason in code's own words (for example 'missing key: stated', or a part marked as not stated by the claim that differs from the default; a key the model added is reported as 'a key that is not allowed', never by its name; a plan the template refuses gets one fixed reason, never the validator's message), stored per attempt with the stage as 'attempt_reasons'; then the run fails before the lock. A change of wording is a new format: a test pins the current format's rendered text of every outcome kind and evidence level. It gives: the question as asked (the claim's words) and as tested (register 'question_as_tested'); the outcome and verdict wording (with the label, exploratory or 'data found; not enough to test'); the evidence level with its wording; when an estimate is shown, the model sentence, the pooled estimate with its unit, its standard error, the p-value phrase, the record and alloy counts and the four paper figures together, the direction note, the spread of the slope information ('an effective number of groups of E out of N informative groups; largest share S', whenever its figures exist, also for a coefficient without inference; compared only with the run's own informative-group count, no threshold, never with a minimum), the group definition, one sensitivity line (sets in agreement, range of estimates with units) and the calibration summary; a coefficient without inference is shown as the coefficient only; when no coefficient could be fitted, no number of it is shown, only that it could not be fitted and how many records of the set could not be used. name: The run order and what a failure does to a run
statement: A run goes: Planner, narrowing decision (code), then either the partly-sufficient path or, after a named person's confirmation of the question as tested (the run waits for it; step 9a), the rules lock, records, Checks, Critic, Inclusion, dataset freeze, statistics, Analyst and the copy of code's decision. A fixed-plan run bypasses the Planner (criterion 14.1a); so does a narrower question's run, recognised by its link to its original (its stored plan), which also waits for the confirmation. A Planner failure, a domain mismatch, a claim that is not one plan, a refused checkpoint or write, changed source versions for a narrower question, and a spending refusal at the Planner or the Critic fail the run with a stated reason. A Critic failure leaves flags unclassified and the run goes on. Any Analyst failure, a spending refusal included, leaves code's decision standing: the run completes with 'explanation unavailable' (a departure from PRD 14.4's 'marked failed' for a cap reached at the Analyst, by the owner's decision). A recording or reservation failure at any agent stops the run at once: no further model request (no further Critic batch, no Analyst), nothing more written, no narrower question created; the run stays running (a call whose recording failed stays started) until recovery takes it up (register 'recovery_policy', step 9b). Taken up again, the run reads each agent's latest stored stage whatever its status, so such a stop, a stage left running or a stored spending refusal has the same effect as when it happened (register 'resumable_run'). No model call runs inside a database transaction.

name: The run waits at the rules lock for a named person
statement: A run whose plan comes from a model's answer waits before its rules lock, with status 'waiting', until a named person confirms the question as tested: a run with a Planner stage (after code's narrowing decision to proceed), and a narrower question's run (its outcome and exclusion rules come from its original's Planner answer). A fixed-plan run of an ordinary question (criterion 14.1a) never waits. Before anything is recorded the person is shown, from stored rows only: the original question, the question as tested, what was narrowed and why, each scope part marked stated or assumed, the outcome, the exclusion rules, the sufficiency option, the fingerprint of the plan to be locked, the source versions and the cost so far; the confirmation stores that content and the exact text shown. The database enforces this too: the confirmation takes one advisory lock that registering a source and sealing a version also take, then checks the registered sources, so a registration and a confirmation cannot slip past each other (fix round 1, finding 2). name: The queue: claims and the heartbeat
statement: A worker claims one run at a time: on its own autocommit lease connection it takes, without waiting, a session advisory lock on the run (CLAIM) and checks that the run's WORK lock is free; then, in one transaction under the run's lock, it re-checks the run, closes a stale open claim as 'lost', records its claim (run_claim; one open claim per run) and starts the run (queued, or a confirmed waiting run, becomes running). The guarded child holds the run's WORK lock for its whole work; an orphan child holding it keeps every worker off the run. A claim's heartbeat is written every 15 seconds by a thread of the worker on the claim row, never the run row, so it never waits behind the run's lock (a named exception to the locking protocol, like audit rows). Each beat also confirms ownership: the beat touched the open claim's row and the lease session still holds CLAIM; otherwise the worker stops its child at once and gives the run up ('lost'). The child's work is bound to its claim: every write checks, in its own transaction after the run's lock, that the claim is open (its row locked FOR KEY SHARE; closing a claim locks the row FOR UPDATE first, so a takeover waits for a write in progress or the write sees the claim closed) and that the child's work lock is still held; a reservation checks the same before any request, and finishing a model call checks the same in its own transaction after the run's lock (fix round 2): a stale child cannot finish its call, which stays started and is closed by recovery as interrupted, counted at its maximum. A stale owner is refused ('claim_lost') before any further write, request or call record (fix round 1, finding 3; fix round 2, finding 1). A claim is taken to be dead when its heartbeat is older than 120 seconds; a claim released for recovery or at shutdown is claimable at once. Running runs are taken up first, then confirmed waiting runs, then queued runs in the order of dispatch. The worker parent never imports dspy, litellm or scipy (it does load numpy, through the source adapters' spreadsheet library).

name: A stuck child
statement: The worker kills its child, releases the claim as 'child_stuck' and lets recovery take the run up when no progress has been seen for 900 seconds since the later of the child's launch and the last progress (downtime before the attempt does not count; fix round 1, finding 6), or after 1,800 seconds in all. Progress is the run's last write (a status change, a stage or call started or finished, a source searched, a record stored, the confirmation, the lock, the freeze), sampled by a thread of the worker with each query cut off after 5 seconds; the worker's main thread never waits for it, so the whole-run limit and the shutdown check keep their own clock (finding 5). 900 seconds covers one agent call's two requests at the 300-second request timeout plus 300 seconds of margin. A deploy (SIGTERM) stops the child (a SIGTERM not obeyed within 10 seconds is escalated to SIGKILL) and releases the claim as 'shutdown'. On every exit path the child is stopped and reaped before the claim is released, and no child is started once shutdown was asked for (finding 2).

statement: When a worker claims a run that is already running, recovery first closes every open model call as 'interrupted' (counted at its reserved maximum under every cap) and every running stage as failed: with the spending refusal recorded against its request when there is one (the refusal and its record are one transaction), else 'interrupted' (fix round 1, finding 1). It writes no plan, record, set, freeze or confirmation. The run then goes on by the normal path, by cause (owner, 2026-10-08): an interruption, a recording failure or any database failure while saving a call, of a stage stored before the recovery, follows the per-role rule (a failure of an agent run after the recovery stops the run normally; finding 4) (the Planner is repeated once, a second loss fails the run; the Critic's remaining batches are skipped; after the Analyst the run completes with 'explanation unavailable'); a spending refusal stays a stop, exactly as in 9a (the Planner and the Critic fail the run, the Analyst completes it; no further request, never a later paid stage). name: Splitting table rows the parser merged
